title: 無機化学
subtitle: Inorganic Chemistry
keywords: Electron configuration 2.Atomic orbitals 3.Chemical bonds 4.Crystal structures 5.Acids and bases
educationalGoal: Students will learn the basics of inorganic chemistry, such as atomic structure (electron configuration, atomic orbitals), chemical bonding, and crystal structures, and the technical terms used in inorganic chemistry. In addition, students will learn about chemical properties that can be explained theoretically by examining the electronic structure. Concepts and theories acquired in this course are the minimum necessary for understanding the properties and reactivity of inorganic compounds.
advice: Students will learn essential concepts in modern inorganic chemistry, with the goal of gaining an understanding of the structure and properties of a variety of inorganic compounds without the need for a teacher. 1. Structure of atoms: electron configuration and atomic orbitals, the periodic table and element blocks 2. Chemical bonding and structures: covalent bonding and Lewis structures, ionic bonds, metal bonds, van der Waals bonds, hydrogen bonds; atomic radius and ion radius, lanthanide contraction, Born-Harber cycle, Mardelung constant, metal crystals; ionic crystals (rock salts, cesium chloride types, zinc blende type); ionization energy, electron affinity, electronegativity 3. Reactions: definitions of acid and base (Arrhenius, Brsted-Lowry, Lewis), HSAB
requiredKnowledge: Pay attention to units as you solve calculation problems. Bring a scientific calculator.

activityGoals.body: Describe electron configurations and atomic orbitals for each element on the periodic table.
Explain trends in ionic radius and electronegativity from the periodic table.
Calculate lattice energy using the Born-Harber cycle.
Describe representative crystal structures and their relation to the ionic radius ratio.
Explain the principles of X-ray diffraction and calculate d from θ and reflection index.
Define the different types of acids and bases, including Arrhenius, Bronsted, and Lewis types.

achievementLevels.ideal: Can solve the entrance examination problems of graduate schools and the employment examination problems of chemical companies and civil servants, which generally involve concepts of inorganic chemistry, such as electron configurations, atomic structures, electronegativity, ionization energy, atomic radius, ionic radius, atomic orbitals, molecular orbitals, and the different definitions of acids and bases.
achievementLevels.standard: Can solve the entrance examination problems of graduate schools, which generally involve concepts of inorganic chemistry, such as electron configurations, atomic structures, electronegativity, ionization energy, atomic radius, ionic radius, atomic orbitals, molecular orbitals, and the different definitions of acids and bases, with the use of textbooks, reference books and dictionaries.

lessons.content: What is inorganic chemistry? Understanding atomic orbitals, Pauli's exclusion principle, and Hund's rule in atomic electron configurations
lessons.assignments: Read the syllabus and learn technical terms that you do not understand.

lessons.content: Understanding the relation between electron configuration and orbital energy levels. Learning how to express covalent bonds using the Lewis structure.
lessons.operation: Lecture, Exercises, Discussion, and Quiz Self-check
lessons.assignments: Describe electron configuration when atomic number is known.

lessons.content: Understanding that atomic radius and ionic radius are affected by the effective nuclear charge, and, for the sixth period, by the lanthanide contraction.
lessons.operation: Lecture, Exercises, Discussion, and Quiz Self-check
lessons.assignments: Explain trends in atomic radius and ion radius changes in relation to the periodic table.

lessons.content: What is the Madelung constant? Understanding the crystal structures of ionic crystals such as NaCl and CsCl, and of metal crystals, such as hcp, fcc (ccp), bcc.
lessons.operation: Lecture, Exercises, Discussion, and Quiz Self-check
lessons.assignments: Describe representative crystal structures of ionic crystals and metal crystals.

lessons.content: Understanding the radius ratio rule for ionic crystals to determine coordination number and stable crystal structure.
lessons.operation: Lecture, Exercises, Discussion, and Quiz Self-check
lessons.assignments: Calculate the radius ratio range for the representative structures of ionic crystals.

lessons.content: Understanding trends in ionic radius, atomic radius, and ionization potential in the periodic table, and their relation to effective nuclear charge.
lessons.operation: Lecture, Exercises, Discussion, and Quiz Self-check
lessons.assignments: Explain trends in ionic radius, atomic radius, and ionization potential from the periodic table.

lessons.content: Understanding the definition of electronegativity, which can be calculated from ionization potential and electron affinity.
lessons.operation: Lecture, Exercises, Discussion, and Quiz Self-check

lessons.content: Understanding the concept of molecular orbitals, including bonding and antibonding orbitals that are formed by overlapping of wave functions.
lessons.operation: Lecture, Exercises, Discussion, and Quiz Self-check
lessons.assignments: Describe the molecular orbital energy level diagrams of N2 and O2.

lessons.content: Understanding the molecular orbital energy level diagrams of H2, N2, O2, and NO molecules.
lessons.operation: Lecture, Exercises, Discussion, and Quiz Self-check
lessons.assignments: Explain why O2 and NO molecules are paramagnetic.

lessons.content: Learning how to use thermodynamic concepts. Understanding the use of the equation, ΔG = ΔH - TΔS.
lessons.operation: Lecture, Exercises, Discussion, and Quiz Self-check
lessons.assignments: Determine whether reactions proceed spontaneously using the equation, ΔG = ΔH - TΔS.

lessons.content: Understanding the meaning of unit cell, lattice plane, and translational symmetry, and the relation among plane index, d, and 2 theta in X-ray diffractometry.
lessons.operation: Lecture, Exercises, Discussion. and Quiz Self-check
lessons.assignments: Calculate the angle at which the diffraction peak appears using Bragg's equation.

lessons.content: Learning about electron-deficient compounds, such as B2H6 and hypervalent compounds such as XeF2 based on oxidation number.
lessons.operation: Lecture, Exercises, Discussion, and Quiz Self-check
lessons.assignments: Calculate the oxidation numbers of various inorganic compounds.

lessons.content: Understanding the three types of acids and bases by Arrhenius, Brsted, and Lewis, and how to calculate pH from pKa (pKb) of an acid (base).
lessons.operation: Lecture, Exercises, Discussion, and Quiz Self-check
lessons.assignments: Calculate pH of mixed solutions of an acid and base using pKa and pKb.
Identify your mistakes and review your weaknesses. Self-reflection

lessons.content: Understanding the principle of hard and soft acids and bases (HSAB).
lessons.operation: Lecture, Exercises, Discussion, and Quiz Self-check
lessons.assignments: Classify acids and bases on the basis of the HSAB principle.
